data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 conflates write-atomicity with resumption safety. Its causal mechanism only ensures that no write is interrupted, then leaps to 'resumption is always safe provided the reservation protocol was followed.' But clean event boundaries do not guarantee the system can produce coherent continuation events: non-deterministic state consumed during reasoning (sampling, tool responses, external API outputs) may have influenced which event was generated next, and if that state is not captured in the event log, resumed events will follow a different trajectory even though every individual write was atomic. The problem asks for conditions under which resumption does not corrupt the append-only IDENTITY of recorded events — not merely their structural integrity. A resumed run that appends structurally valid but trajectory-incoherent events corrupts the identity of the event sequence as a single coherent run. SRC_002's refusal cases address only protocol violations and estimate errors, never the case where the reservation protocol was perfectly followed but non-deterministic reasoning state was lost. Furthermore, the entire answer is conditional on one specific design (per-event reservation), providing no conditions for systems that do not use that protocol, which the problem does not assume.
